utterances.text: In fact, if I can direct your attention, sir, on Exhibit 670, to the end of the fourth paragraph, there's a statement made: "Every flag that they see in passing will remind them that this is the living space of the Croatian people." Then continuing on: "Therefore, let us be conscientious and display our flags."

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to Travnik then, in fact, to investigate an incident where two Muslim soldiers had been killed, related to it an incident about the flying of the Croatian flag; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're at paragraph 95.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and your ECMM colleague then went on to Travnik to try to determine what the situation was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to get through the HVO checkpoint there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Actually, I cannot remember if we were allowed to pass the checkpoint or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on your way there? This was an HVO checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. At the junction on the way to Novi Travnik and Travnik, there was an HVO checkpoint at that spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these appear to you to be what you might call regular HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, there was HVO soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there appear to you to be some other soldiers there that you knew or sometimes referred to by -- not only you but other International Community members referred to sometimes as HOS, H-O-S, soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. We saw HOS soldiers there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you know about the HOS soldiers at the time? They were there at the same checkpoint, at the same time, with the HVO soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct. We even passed -- on our way to the checkpoint, we passed a headquarter where we were able to see that HOS were in the area, because they were showing the Croatian flag and they were showing the flag that was normally used by HOS units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that flag for us?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Just like a pirate flag with -- a black flag with a skull and with bones -- crossbones on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you know about these HOS soldiers in terms of who they were at that time? I mean, what type of a unit were they? Did they dress differently?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: They dressed differently. Normally they were wearing black uniforms. We knew that in the beginning HOS units, they were specially trained units, and in the beginning, the HOS units were apart of HVO and a part of BiH, but at this time, I think that other HOS units were belonging to HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "specially trained units" or special units, in what way did you understand them to be special?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I think they had a special training for -- and were units used for special purposes. So they were able to do other things than just be normal soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your time in Central Bosnia, did you and other ECMM members come to have any understanding of any particular role, if any, that these special units played in connection with some of the events, the more notorious events in Central Bosnia that you became involved in investigating?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We often learned that when we came to an area where there had been some killings of civilians, it was often HOS units who were behind that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going on to about the 13th or 14th of April, 1993, there was an event, was there not, where four HVO officers were kidnapped in the Travnik area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the HVO made one of these types of protests or complaints to the Busovaca Joint Commission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then around the same time, on about the 15th of April, the commander of the HVO Jure Francetic Brigade, Zivko Totic, was kidnapped in Zenica. His car was stopped and his four bodyguards were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct. And an eyewitness in the area was killed as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did RC Zenica subsequently become involved in investigating these events?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Busovaca Joint Commission made a team and ordered this team to investigate in the matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before continuing on, would you look at Exhibit 635.1?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It should be the next document on top of everyone's bundle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 635.1, is this a copy of the daily operational report from the Busovaca Joint Commission?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I meant to point this out to you sooner and I passed it. Paragraphs 1 and 4, does this talk about, in fact, these problems with the demonstrations of the Croatian flag and some of the incidents that had been caused about that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, item (B) talks about: "The shooting incident last evening in Travnik." That's one of the incidents you were talking about a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Friis-Pedersen, the chairman of the Busovaca Joint Commission, about at this time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then going on to Exhibit 693. Again, this report covers a broad area of the ECMM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Court will see, everyone will see there are many reports from different regions and groups, but directing your attention to page 4, paragraph 16 -- well, there is a number there, 16.4, I guess, because that's the date. I'm sorry, just the bottom of page 4. This composite report includes the reports from RC Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting at the bottom of page 4. For instance, on page 5, under the heading -- near the heading -- sub-heading "Novi Travnik," there is the reference to the preliminary work concerning the four kidnapped HVO officers. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And jumping all the way down to paragraph -- excuse me, page 10. At page 10 of the document, again in reference to the sub-heading "Zenica," there's a report concerning the kidnapping of the officer Totic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back to the first entry with that background, on page 4, was it the assessment of RC Zenica, as reported up the ECMM chain of command, on the 16th of April, 1993, again I'm looking at the bottom of page 4: "Situation is very tense in Central Bosnia with open fighting in the Vitez and Jablanica areas. The two sides appear to be reluctant to enter into substantial negotiations for ceasefire. Seems that both sides are determined to size ..." I'm going to suggest, Your Honour, that should be "seize,". "... or protect whatever they believe belongs to them in order to strengthen their position in future negotiations." Was that the ECMM assessment on the 16th of April, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one matter we were considering. Going back to Exhibit 2574, the newspaper report of the Vance-Owen Plan, you remember that we have had other documents setting out the plan and other maps of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be that no one can answer this at the moment, but does the newspaper report, in fact, reflect the plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can't answer that question myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, Major Baggesen, whether the report, the newspaper article, if you will, that accompanied -- or that this map was part of, described or gave some account of the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't suppose at this length of time the witness can possibly remember, but in fact, if you look at Exhibit 1658, there we have the plan, which I think was taken from the evidence earlier. I don't want to waste time now. Perhaps somebody could have a look over the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe -- if it's 1658, the map is substantially the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, that's my impression, but perhaps someone can have a look. If there is any difference, we can be told.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I would regard it as very useful not just to have the plan itself, but that part of it which indicates the racial composition, the mixture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure we can provide that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we can finish with Exhibit 693, Major. On the bottom of page 4 -- I'm sorry. Excuse me, I lost my place. On about the middle of page 5, in reference to the paragraph headed "Zenica," let me direct your attention, please, to a couple of sentences into that paragraph and ask you if this is correct, and not only correctly written but, in fact, was the assessment that you were familiar with at that time on the ground. I'm looking at the language that says, "ECMM is trying hard to relax the tension, but both sides, especially in the higher military level, are not willing to take part in negotiations before the achievement of their political and military objectives."

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your personal assessment at the time as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm looking at the clock. I'm at the Court's pleasure. I'm about to start a different topic. We can start it and break any time, or if the Court wishes, we could stop now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Basically paragraph 102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can deal with those two matters very briefly, 102 and 103, and we'll stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we have talked in the last few minutes, sir, that there were these -- among other things, I'm sure -- these two particular incidents concerning the HVO officers. And is it correct that the regional deputy chief of ECMM, Mr. Juan Valentin, and you, yourself, formed a Busovaca Joint Commission team with Dzemal Merdan and Franjo Nakic to investigate these incidents?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And together with us, we had some of the local civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of this, did your group, as just described, travel to Novi Travnik and Bugojno --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to visit the Muslim 7th Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct. The reason for us to visit the 7th Muslim Brigade was that the HVO thought that this 7th Muslim Brigade was a unit that was behind the kidnapping of the four HVO officers in Travnik and of the HVO brigade commander in Zenica. That's the reason why we visited the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, then, Your Honour, if we could stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now until half past 2.00. Major, would you remember, please, during this and any other adjournment, not to speak to anybody about your evidence. Don't let anybody speak to you about it, and of course that includes members of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you please be back at half past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 24 25

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we start with the witness, I think I can answer the Court's question, at least in part. The map on 2574, the newspaper map, is in all respects the same as 1658, save this -- and when I say that, I'm referring to the map on the top of 1658 -- in the newspaper map, the municipalities of Vares and Visoko have been grouped with Sarajevo, whereas in the map which is part of 1658, they are included in proposed province 9. I'm afraid, at the moment, I can't offer you any particular explanation for that except it is the way the map literally did evolve over time. We can find the answer to that, but those are the only differences between those two maps as we can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Major Baggesen, we had left off, you and an ECMM are -- actually, a Busovaca Joint Commission team, including the HVO representative and the ABiH representative, had gone to Novi Travnik and Bugonjo to investigate, and you were on your way back, and is it correct that on your way back from that trip you were stopped -- you stopped, yourself, in Novi Travnik to give a report to the local HVO commander there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What made you think to stop and give this report?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We wanted to tell the local brigade commander about our findings because, as far as I can remember, the four staff officers were from his brigade command. Therefore, we wanted to tell him about our findings just so the level of information was the best as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of that meeting, is it correct, sir, that the local commander of the HVO military police came into the meeting, was very unhappy with you and the others that you had not, by that date, found the kidnapped officers or their kidnappers, and said that the only solution, in his view, was to arrest Dzemal Merdan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he, in fact, arrest Dzemal Merdan at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the HVO officers with you are present, both the Travnik -- Novi Travnik commander and Franjo Nakic were surprised at his action but essentially said that they could not stop it because they didn't have the authority to control this military police officer?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, they said that. They said the only one who was able to give orders to the military police commander was Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you protest the arrest of General Merdan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did, because when Mr. Merdan was travelling together with us in the Busovaca Joint Commission team, he was a member of the team and he was under our protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that result then in you and your ECMM colleague likewise being placed under arrest?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an HVO guard put on you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: After that, of course, I made another protest. Then I asked Sabljic, to use his phone, and I tried to get in contact with Colonel Blaskic, and I tried to get in contact with my own headquarters to tell them about the new situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were you able to it reach anyone at UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Not at that time, because we were not able to get in contact with UNPROFOR, but we asked our headquarter in Zenica to get in contact with UNPROFOR, to the British Battalion in Vitez, and to ask them to come and rescue us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that when you told the military police commander that UNPROFOR would, in fact, come to retrieve you, that the police commander was very unhappy?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, he told us that if UNPROFOR units would try to come and help us out, his units would open fire against the UNPROFOR units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to, after that point, in fact, reach Colonel Blaskic on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We tried to get in contact with Colonel Blaskic. I can remember we were not able on the first try because he was not present at his office, but he was in the building somewhere. On our second try, we were able to get in contact with Colonel Blaskic, and we told him about the situation, and he asked to speak with the HVO commander, and he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the "HVO commander," this was the --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No, the military police commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened as a result of the conversation between the military police commander and Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: At the beginning of the conversation, it took place at Mr. Sabljic's office. We had been there the whole time. But after awhile, the military police officer didn't want to speak with Colonel Blaskic in that office, so he went to another office and continued his conversation with Colonel Blaskic, and after awhile he came back and released us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his appearance when he came back into the room?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: He was red-faced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released at that time, including Dzemal Merdan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around this same time did Colonel Blaskic order, to your knowledge, the HVO to close the road between Gornji Vakuf and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to return then to Zenica after that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: After that time we were able to continue our travel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 15th of April, 1993, is it correct that a Canadian ECMM monitor named Remi Landry joined you in continuing to investigate these several incidents?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He replaced Juan Valentin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Vitez, the two of you, and spend the night in Vitez, on the night of the 15th of April, instead of returning to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jumping outside of the chronology but not to leave the five HVO officers, a part of the story, unresolved, is it correct, sir, that some weeks after this that all five of the HVO officers were released unharmed as part of an ECMM arranged prisoner release?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Mr. Kordic was present at this ceremony or event when the HVO officers were released?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That, I think, is in dispute, is it? Is it in dispute? I seem to have a note to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honour. It's my mistake. I apologise. I missed my own note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, Major Baggesen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could describe -- Major, were you present when the HVO officers were released?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And can you tell us who was there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: It was -- this incident with the kidnapped officers, we investigated that and we found out that the kidnappers were not BiH but the Mujahedins in the area, and as the Prosecutor told you, ECMM and UNPROFOR were there to release them after we had been having some meetings with the Mujahedins. I was responsible for releasing of the four HVO officers from the Novi Travnik area or the Travnik area, and the four officers were handed over to me by the Mujahedins at a secret place, and from there, with an escort from the police battalion, I took them to Vitez, to the Hotel Vitez, where Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Kordic were present. And then the four officers were handed over to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly when that was? If the kidnapping was the 13th, 14th of April, is it possible to say roughly how long after the kidnapping this event occurred?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I think it was after a month or something. But we have it somewhere in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can probably provide an ECMM report about that. I don't have it with me today, but I think it will indicate that it was approximately three or four weeks after --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I can find it in my diary, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just point the major to May the 17th in his diary, I think that's -- is that when it was?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Monday, the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your testimony, Major Baggesen, is that Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Kordic were part of -- would it be called a reception committee, if you will?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: A welcome commission. And as far as I can remember, it was covered by the local TV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back to our chronology --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Unless the Court has other questions about that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and Mr. Landry had spent the night in Vitez, the night between the 15th and 16th of April. Is it correct, sir, that on the morning of the 16th of April, about 5.30, you woke up to the sounds of artillery fire; you realised that there was heavy fighting going on and that some of the firing was close to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could hear firing from heavy machine guns, and heard that both the artillery fire and the mortar fire was what might be described as outgoing? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a military person, perhaps any military person, you can tell the Court, and as someone trained in artillery, how could you tell that this was outgoing fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Because when a mortar or artillery is firing, you can hear the noise from that. It's different from the impact; it's not the same noise or the same sound. So there is no doubt for us as trained military persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also tell, or have at least a -- or make an assessment as to what this was the type of artillery or mortars that were being used?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: From what we were able to hear, it was medium artillery, either medium or heavy mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both the sound -- both the fact that the sounds were of outgoing fire and the nature of the weapons being used, did that help you come to any conclusion about who was doing the firing?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, because we knew that the HVO had positions around in the area, so it was obvious that it was from the HVO positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or ECMM have any information around that time that the ABiH forces in the Vitez area were armed with that type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We have no information on that. UNPROFOR had patrols in the area, and we had patrols in that area, and we had never seen any signs of Armija, BiH, positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that to your knowledge, or the ECMM's knowledge, the ABiH forces, if at all, were armed with either small arms or light machine guns?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: At that time, in that area, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, sir, that you and Mr. Landry decided to leave for Zenica right away, about 6.00 on the morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you went to an HVO checkpoint in Dubravica, and on the way there you came upon a circle of five Muslim civilians who were lying on the road --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- stomach down? And what did you do at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Just after we passed them, we stopped our vehicle, and we would have liked to go out to see if these men still were alive, or what had -- try to monitor the situation, try to find out what has been happening there. But when we went out of our vehicles, we were shot at, so we were forced back to our vehicle and forced out of that area again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, as you proceeded on down the road, were you stopped at an HVO checkpoint at Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that an HVO -- was that checkpoint manned by HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Then we had to go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went back to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many HVO soldiers do you recall being at this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I can recall that there were more than normal. As I can remember, there were maybe ten or more in that area, and normally there was only two or maybe three soldiers manning this checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the increased manpower at the checkpoint mean anything to your -- impress you as having any particular significance?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: It showed us that something was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Later on the 16th of April, 1993, about 9.30 in the evening, did you and Mr. Landry decide to make another attempt to drive from Vitez to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We were able to see that there was still fighting in the area. We were able to see that -- when we were passing Vitez, we could see a lot of burning houses in the old part of Vitez. We were able to pass the Dubravica checkpoint, and when we continued, we were able to see that the whole sky over Ahmici was totally illuminated by a big fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: And when we were passing Ahmici, we were able to see that it looked like -- that the whole area was burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before we come back to Ahmici, when you passed by, and you said the area of -- in Stari Vitez was -- there was a lot of firing and some houses on fire there, was Stari Vitez the portion of Vitez where primarily the Muslim community lived?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at Exhibit 2193, which is one of the photographs that's in the packet that was at the bottom of the bundle, Your Honour, and again, it's marked in the lower right corner as 2193. THE USHER: 2193?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yeah, 2193. Perhaps you can put that on the ELMO so that we can see -- when you point out things on the map, everyone will be able to see what it is you're pointing to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, have you marked on this -- this is an aerial photo of Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you marked on this map the checkpoints that you encountered on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Actually those checkpoints marking this map were some permanent checkpoints. Those checkpoints were there before this incident that we're ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did there continue to be checkpoints at these locations on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you refer to the one that's farthest to the top of the page and further to the left. What particular traffic did that checkpoint have the ability to control, if you will?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: The checkpoint I mentioned as HVO checkpoint 2 was able to control the road down to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, just hold on one moment, please. I think we're looking at two different -- just so the record is clear, let's start with the other one, the other checkpoint, higher on the page would be approximately 10.00 or 11.00 --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Okay. That's the Dubravica checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What traffic does that checkpoint control?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Controls the traffic coming from the two roads, one of the roads is what we were calling the mountain road to Zenica, and the checkpoint was controlling the other road as well. So by manning this checkpoint you were able to control the junction and the traffic coming into that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's go to what's been marked as HVO CP 2. What additional or different traffic, if any, is controlled at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: This checkpoint controlled the traffic from the main road into Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on this second attempt, when you and Mr. Landry left Vitez at 9.30 that evening, you were able to get through both checkpoints; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were just about to tell us a few minutes ago, when you got to Ahmici, you could see that essentially the entire sky was on fire because the village was burning?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We were trying to get into Ahmici, to monitor the situation, but we were stopped at the checkpoint on one of the roads going to Ahmici, and we were not allowed to go in there. This was an HVO checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, before we get to that particular checkpoint, when you approached Ahmici, is it correct, sir, that you could not only see the fires burning but you could also see machine gun fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the tracers from the machine gun fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We could see the tracers, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there tracer fire in both directions or tracer fire only from one direction?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Only from one direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you knew about the disposition of forces at that time, from what side was the machine gun fire coming? You saw no return fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No return fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw that the village was on fire, could you at that time see that the minaret on the mosque was still standing?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: At that time it was still standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Court what that looked like to you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Actually, it was an awful sight, because we could see the minaret and we could see all the -- the whole sky around the minaret was totally in flames.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you come to know, sometime shortly before this, from one of your interpreters, that the mosque -- that particular mosque in Ahmici had just been built or renovated a short time before this?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was told that. A few days before I went to Ahmici actually just to see the mosque, because the people in Ahmici were very proud of this mosque. Therefore, I went up to see the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that the Muslims in Ahmici actually raised the money to build or renovate this mosque themselves?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I was told that. When we were at Ahmici, everything was calm in Ahmici. There was no sign of military activity in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How soon before the 16th of April had you been in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date, but I think it was a few days before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be in your diary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: For the moment, do we need that date? If it's a few days before, that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Major, don't bother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you able to reach an -- make an assessment, based on what you could see of the village burning, how those fires had been started? If you can make that kind of assessment, then tell the Court what you base that on.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: The fire in Ahmici was not a result of the shelling against the area, so we concluded that because there was so many houses that were burning, that someone had put fire to the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you tell that it wasn't caused by shelling?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Because normally if it was a result of shelling, you would be able to see it on the roof on the houses because then all the tiles would have been blown off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There would be artillery damage to the houses themselves?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you saw these houses burning they were essentially intact houses that were on fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: What we were able to see from our position outside the town, because we were not allowed to go into the town. But we were able to see some of the houses from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to Exhibit Z1585, which should be the next -- I hope, the next photograph in the packet of oversized materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't have the packet of oversized materials, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's it. I see what Judge Robinson has, Your Honour. If not, we'll certainly provide more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on Exhibit 1585, Major Baggesen, can you indicate where -- when you attempted -- when you and Mr. Landry attempted to enter Ahmici on the night of the 16th of April, where was the checkpoint where you were stopped?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We were stopped in the checkpoint situated here [indicates], and we were able to look up at this road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the -- you were on the main road between Vitez and Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's the road running out here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the turnoff, at least, is oriented on this particular photograph, the turnoff to the left, leaves the main road and goes up into the village of Ahmici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the HVO -- well, did the HVO soldier tell you that the reason that he would not allow you and Mr. Landry going up into the village was because there was too much fighting?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We were told there was heavy fighting in the area and it was actually because of our own security we were not allowed in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the advantage point that you and Mr. Landry had, could you see any actual fighting in the village at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see what appeared to the persons or bodies lying on the ground?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: From our positions in the checkpoint we were able to see persons on the ground, lying on the ground. We were not able to see if they were alive or dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that you were surprised by these events, what you saw happening in Ahmici and the surrounding area on the 16th of April, because ECMM had not seen any sign of actual fighting between the HVO and the ABiH in that area up about that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Because when I went to Ahmici a few days before, there was no signs of any military activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: There was no fortifications, there was no barbed wire, there were no soldiers around. There was only civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you travelled around the Vitez-Zenica area on the 16th of April, you and Mr. Landry, is it correct, sir, that you only saw -- the only soldiers you saw that day were HVO and HOS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout your travels on that day you did not see any Bosnian government forces or Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it appear to you, sir, that the HVO had effectively sealed off the Vitez area, with all traffic being controlled in and out?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, because all the checkpoints were heavily manned, more than normal, so we concluded that they had sealed the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention and the Court's attention to Exhibit 2613, which again is another map in the packet. On this map have you previously marked various checkpoints, some belonging to the HVO and some belonging to the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Those checkpoints were, say, the normal picture of checkpoints before and after this episode.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you testified a moment ago, can you tell the Court that based upon your knowledge of the area, by these particular HVO checkpoints could you effectively control access into the Vitez area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Those two checkpoints here were the checkpoints I showed before on the aerial photograph [indicates], and they are controlling the road from Zenica to Vitez, through the mountains. There was a checkpoint in the Kaonik area, and that checkpoint was controlling all the traffic coming from east [indicates]. There was a checkpoint near Travnik controlling all traffic coming from Travnik and from the Novi Travnik area [indicates]. At that time, I don't have any information concerning HVO checkpoints in this area [indicates], but we learned later on that there were some checkpoints up here, but I don't know exactly where they were. So they were able to control all the traffic into that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just for point of reference and while we have this map in front us, if you go to the HVO marked checkpoints, the two in Vitez at approximately the lower middle of the page, can you point out to the -- if you'll go out about 3.00, probably about four -- maybe four centimetres or so from about 3.00 there, can you point out Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, Ahmici is situated here [indicates]. Actually, between those checkpoints here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the HVO effectively controlled access on either side of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if you look, please, again, basically at the 6.00 position below the HVO checkpoint around Kaonik, again, just for purposes of orientation, at the bottom of the map is that the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. So in this area [indicates] they were able to control as well the Busovaca road. The Busovaca road is going from Busovaca and further south and are connected with Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking back on the events of the 16th of April, 1993, did you reach any professional military judgement, sir, on how those attacks were carried out or the nature of those attacks?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: In our opinion, it was a military attack against a civilian target, if you can call this for a target, but it was a military operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you base that on?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Because we only saw HVO in that area, and we didn't see anyone that returned fire against the HVO-controlled area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many -- do you have an estimate of how many soldiers, based upon your military training and experience, how many soldiers would have been required to carry out the operations that you saw in the Vitez-Ahmici area on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Actually, it's a very difficult question to answer, but I think a minimum of 600 men just to seal the area and to do the attack against Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, based on your 20 years of military experience -- and you are the Operations Officer now of your unit in Denmark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would fall to you to plan an operation and carry out an operation like this, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what would go into the organisation and carrying out a military operation involving something like 600 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: You have to do proper planning, because it's not just enough to order the soldiers to go in and make that attack. You have to make an operational order doing that. And this order, there should be orders concerning the logistics, because you have to bring ammunition, you have to bring fuel, you have to bring other things to do an action like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to transport your troops into the area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think, at that time, it was -- to transport the soldiers from -- for example, from Vitez to Ahmici, you don't have to use vehicles for that because of the distance, but normally you have to plan how to use trucks and all that as well. We concluded that this was not only a small unit, because it was too big an incident. So you were not -- it would have to be carried out by more than one small unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you saw happen in Vitez and Ahmici on the 16th of April, could that have been carried out by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is going beyond the military -- I'm sorry. You were going to ask about the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I was looking at 152.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I'm not quite at that point yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that attack or those events have been carried out by a small group of individuals acting as a renegade or individual unit?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without attributing any -- I don't want you to discuss the state of mind of who might have been involved in the attack, but based on your military experience, if you're correct that this was an attack on a civilian population, why would that be done? Why do you attack a civilian population?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think this is a matter for a military officer. This is something that we're going to have to decide, isn't it. We're going to decide what inferences we can draw from the evidence as to why the attack might have taken place, if there was one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me finish up the area this way: Again, both on the 16th and the days leading up to the 16th, you had not seen any Muslim armed forces or preparations in the area of Ahmici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'll go to Exhibit 738, which we're now back into the documentary exhibits as opposed to the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I've skipped, for the moment, 735. It might cause some confusion, but I find in my notes it's either unnecessary or comes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have 738. If I can direct your attention to paragraph 9 on the bottom of page 2. Was the ECMM assessment of this -- and this is a report -- excuse me. This is a report for the week of the 11th to the 18th of April, 1993. It's a weekly summary. On the item that I just directed your attention to, is it correct that it was the ECMM official assessment at that time that the relations in Central Bosnia deteriorated sharply during the week. A possible explanation for the tension in the area could be the suspected aim of the HVO, while the world's attention is focused on Srebrenica and East Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to take over the territory of the two provinces described in the Vance-Owen Plan as predominantly Croat while the Muslim community is determined to avoid this?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think you ought to read the next sentence for the sake of completeness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You also reported that HVO and BiH forces fought openly in Vitez, Zenica, and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And to follow up on the president's question and your testimony a moment ago, there were -- is it correct to say, sir, that there was fighting with Muslim armed forces in that wider Vitez/Zenica/Travnik area, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not around Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Not around Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just as a matter of historical interest, do you recall, with this reference to Srebrenica, do you recall that it was exactly this same time, or this weekend, that was when Srebrenica finally fell?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to paragraph 11 of the next page -- and I'm not going to read this one, but I think everyone has it -- if you will read that to yourself, and again, do you recall that being the ECMM assessment, and did you agree with that assessment?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 813.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I'm only going to -- the conclusions are similar, but this is an ECMM report, Your Honour, the reason why this looks very similar to Exhibit 738. I think that it will just simply show that it's another one of these reports in the chain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in this particular item, directing your attention to paragraph 15 on page 2 on Exhibit 813, and was that your -- directing your attention to paragraph 15, was that your personal -- did you agree with that analysis?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. This was the official ECMM conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where it states, "The declared position of the Bosnian Croat authorities to implement the Vance-Owen Plan, forcing the Muslim population to leave the so-called 'Croat provinces,' provoked a reaction which resulted in strong and brutal fighting, with actions against the civilian population, especially in the Zenica and Vitez regions." Is what you saw in Ahmici and the Vitez area on the 16th of April consistent with that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to briefly touch on three additional exhibits as part of the record, without spending a lot of time on them, but I think this witness is able to identify them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can look at Exhibit 719, which is titled "Special Report on the Middle Bosnia Situation," do you recall RC Zenica around this time -- this is dated the 18th of April, 1993 -- preparing a report or assessment of the events over the preceding several days --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in Central Bosnia? And just by a point of reference, the handwritten notation toward the lower left-hand part of the page, are those Remi Landry's markings?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the colleague who was with you on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, and this special report is made by him and I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two of you together?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, directing your attention to the third page, does it include both your signature and Mr. Landry's signature?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: On the third page? Yes. And the first two words, "Venlig Hilsen," that's in Danish, and that means "Yours Sincerely."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Because this is not the original. This is a copy, as I was sending to another one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to Exhibit 720, dated the 18th of April, 1993. This is going to ECMM headquarters in Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the purpose of this report, in particular, to relate the statements or allegations that were being made by the head of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina 3rd Corps? And directing your attention to item 3 and carrying on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of the bottom of that page, second page, the initials "J. Valentin," was that the deputy head of the RC Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Dagos was the operations officer?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go to Exhibit 754, this is a report from the Busovaca Joint Commission dated the 20th of April, 1993. Directing your attention to the second page, did you know both of those individuals?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Erik Friis-Pedersen was the head of the Busovaca Commission at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Henk Morsink was a Dutch monitor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there various efforts to establish a cease-fire around the 16th of April and the days thereafter?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Say again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were there various efforts, both by UNPROFOR and by the ECMM, on the 16th of April and in the next few days, trying to establish a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking back to Item 1 on that report, is it correct that -- "In the Vitez area, still very tense and even getting worse in the afternoon, with a lot of firing from positions around the area of BritBat camp. Many refugees with luggage on the streets and snipers everywhere. In Travnik, situation also got more tense from midafternoon, due to firing from many HVO high ground positions around the city"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the morning of the 19th of April, 1993, did you find yourself in the town of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's our headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's our headquarters, in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about 9.30 that morning, did you hear shelling coming into the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, and we were able to see that from our headquarters. We were situated at the Hotel Internacional, and from our window, we were able to see the area that was attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and another ECMM colleague named Allan Laustsen -- who was another Danish monitor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to respond to the area where the shells had exploded?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. After the attack in the afternoon, we went to the area that had been shelled, and we found out that it was the marketplace in Zenica. We were able to see the impacts in the area, and we were able to see the damages in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that 13 civilians were killed and many others injured as a result of this shelling?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the majority of the killed and injured were Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were in the town market at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a Danish officer, have you had training in the use and effects of artillery?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, basic training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Laustsen, wasn't he, in fact, a former Danish artillery officer?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, Laustsen is an artillery officer. He is now a police officer, but he is a reserve officer in the artillery in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We're now going to the separate packet of exhibits, Your Honour. If the witness could look at -- first, starting with Exhibit 2282,1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a photograph that you took in the area of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. That's from the marketplace. And on the opposite side of the road, where all the people from the market were placed, and all the killed and injured people. But I didn't want to take pictures of that, so I just took a picture of this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're looking away from the main impact location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'll go to Exhibit 2282,2, what is that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That shows another impact in the bus stop, just close to the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is that in the picture?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's my colleague, Allan Laustsen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a bus stop?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. There were no buses, so there were no injuries in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go to 2282 -- I'm sorry. Before you go there --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll have to inquire, because there were some additional photographs that were added after the bundles were first handed out, and I don't know whether they made it into your bundle or not. 2277,1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, I've got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Very well. If you have that on the ELMO, 2277,1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this looking back the other direction? What -- the car in the foreground that we see, is that the car that you photographed before?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now we're looking back more toward the marketplace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. On this picture you're able to see all the killed civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: At some stage we need to go through these and make sure we've got them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But we don't want to waste time now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photograph we're looking at now, 2277,1, for instance, there's a body in the middle of the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And over to the right of that body, on the sidewalk, is that one of the areas where there was a principal impact?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll see there's little tables and chairs set up, if you will, along a wall; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's where a number of the civilians were killed? Would you go to Exhibit 2277,2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think, unless there's a particular point the witness can deal with and you want to ask him about, we can see these pictures for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. If we can just go, then, to -- well, let me stop on 2277, because it is a better picture that relates to his further testimony about his crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at 2277,2, Major, that is an impact crater; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some of those markings and the edges of that crater, are those sometimes called "splashmarks"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's from the shrapnel exploding?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we go to Exhibit 2282,3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which is only a Xerox of the photograph, Your Honour, and I apologise for the quality. I'm sure there's a better version that can be obtained at some point, but I'll just simply have the witness describe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was one particular crater that you photographed and looked at with some greater degree of attention and care; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. Specific to this impact that I took the photograph of, because this was one of the impacts where we based our investigations on. On this pact, we were able, with a simple investigation, to see what direction the shell came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before you get to that -- well, I see Mr. Sayers is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think at this point we're coming to paragraphs 158 and 159. The only objection is this: I think that any opinions that the witness may have based upon what he referred to as basic training that he received in artillery, that they require expert opinion and I don't think that he has the expertise necessary to utter those opinions. There is -- his colleague, Mr. Lawson, apparently has some artillery training, and I understand that Mr. Lawson is coming up to testify in the next week or two, so maybe it would be better to have any opinions from him rather than someone who has simply had basic training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, that's a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's a point, Your Honour, but if the content is not contested, Your Honour, I see little point is served not simply saying -- letting this man who has come here to testify about it so say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I gather this is a matter which that is in issue. Is that right, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It is. Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have-- you were with -- you have basically artillery training in the Danish army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Laustsen, who was with you, was an artillery officer?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the two of you, working together, come to a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think he should be able to state it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we don't want to have the evidence twice over when it can be dealt with fairly shortly. We are not bound by complicated rules about qualifications. The witness clearly has some knowledge of artillery matters and, therefore, he can give the evidence but, Mr. Scott, it mustn't be repeated, or if so, it must be repeated in short form.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, you will see here that on the outline that there are basically two or three questions and it will be over in about 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the crater, were you and Mr. Laustsen able to reach an opinion as to the type of artillery that had been used to make these -- fire these rounds?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. We based that on the size of the impact, because your bigger size -- a big impact shows it's a big shell, and a short impact shows it's a small shell. Is that clear enough?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some very basic level. That particular part is no more complicated than that, but how about -- could you tell from there what type of a shell -- gun would have made that kind of an impact, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We conclude that this should be from a 122-millimetre gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon your military experience, what's the approximate range of that kind of artillery weapon?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Up to 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going further, were you able, from looking at the crater and doing some fieldwork, to reach any conclusions about the direction from which the shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a compass -- take a compass reading on the impact?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Not for only this impact but for those impacts in -- for this attack, we took a compass bearing from all the impacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Essentially, you wound up with a composite reading of some sort?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the compass reading that you recall?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Two hundred and seventy degrees. That was from west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge of again the disposition of forces in the area, who controlled the ground from which you determined that shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look at Exhibit 2282,6, which again is a map, Your Honour. Looking at 2282,6, did you draw -- essentially, this is a map of the Zenica locality. There is a line that's been drawn, if you will, out from the left of the city or town of Zenica. Does that indicate to you approximately the direction from which the shells were fired?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. The marketplace is situated here, and using our compass, we were able to see that the firing was from this direction against Zenica, and I suppose that the position was over in this area here, and we knew that this area was under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that area sometimes known generally as the Bila area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Bila area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, based on your training and experience, were you able to see in Zenica that day, on the 19th of April, any military targets in the area of the shell impacts?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No. Actually, we knew where the military targets, as you call them that, were in Zenica, and there was no military targets in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention to Exhibit 2282,4, which, for ease of reference, is this exhibit. Is Exhibit 2282,4 a map or a drawing of the city of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the letter or initial "M" designate, approximately the middle of the document?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's the marketplace where the impacts were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, also around this same map, encircled -- in the circled items, as an example there's a number 11 at approximately the 12.00 position, about six or seven centimetres above the "M" there's a number that's circled 11, and once you see that one -- Your Honour, I'm doing this for everyone's benefit -- you'll see that there are other similar markings around the document. Do those relate to the legend that's provided as part of 2282.5, showing -- and with a code or a key as to what those locations are?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for instance, if we look at item number 1, which is about at the -- well, if you can show -- it's probably -- maybe it's easier for you, on the ELMO, to show where you see item -- it's location 1?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: At the top of the point [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over on the far left edge. And that was the 3rd Corps command or headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the ABiH forces. Now, based on your military training and experience, what would be a reasonable margin of error for a well-trained gun crew firing something like a 122 millimetre piece of artillery at a range of up to 15 kilometres? What would you expect some reasonable, if we can call it that, margin of error would be?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: If we have to compare it with trained artillery personnel?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I think 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'd expect a well-trained gun crew to be able to hit a target within approximately 50 metres of the aim point?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would be a margin of error for a much -- a not so well-trained gun crew?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I think at the top 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, looking at Exhibit 2282,4, what's the distance on this map between the shell impacts in the marketplace and what you would have considered, based on your knowledge, the closest military target?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: The closest military target is number 5. There's approximately 500 metres from this area to the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Five hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Five hundred metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about five times the margin of error for even a badly trained crew; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. And actually, when you are firing a artillery gun, the most difficult is not the sideways but it's to shoot long enough, because it's very easy to point a gun in the right direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not -- you're saying it's not so much whether the shell's to the left or right but whether it's either short or over the target?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your professional military judgement, Major, was there any -- was there any military target within a reasonable margin of error to the impact point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. I don't think that's a fair question. We've heard the evidence which the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. If I can just have a moment, Your Honour. I think some of this we've now covered in the course of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just to finish on Zenica then, the shelling was into the town marketplace at about 9.30 on the morning of April 19th, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. And the ECMM had a conclusion on this attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you state, that please?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: ECMM concluded that this attack was not against a military target but against a civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to Exhibit 757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, when you get to a convenient moment, we'll adjourn, perhaps when you finish this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Adjourn for the day, Your Honour, or for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. I think we can cover this exhibit in fairly short order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another of the ECMM reports, is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And directing your attention to the last page, this is signed by someone named Brix-Andersen?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Brix-Andersen?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Ole Brix-Andersen was a Danish Ambassador sitting at our headquarter in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
