utterances.text: Looking at the text of this report, approximately a little over one and a half pages, I take it much of this report would, in fact, have been written at the level of RC Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you or Mr. Landry or Mr. Laustsen, in fact, had a hand in preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I think this report is made on conclusions of -- on our reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So again, you would have done your daily reports and then people above you, such as Mr. Thebault or others, would have consolidated those reports into another report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report sent from Brix-Andersen to the Danish Minister of Foreign Affairs, because at that time Denmark had chairmanship in the EC, and that's why Brix-Andersen is sending his report to a Danish government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, I'm sure everyone knows, but when you say the "EC" you're talking about the -- what was then the European Community?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of conclusions and assessments stated in this document, would you agree with them, sir, and were they consistent with your observations in Central Bosnia in the middle of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think we can stop there, Your Honour, for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're moving on to a new topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall be sitting until quarter to 5.00. We will adjourn for ten minutes now. I see you've got quite a bit to do, but if you can complete the witness today so we may start cross-examination tomorrow, it may allow the witness to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll push on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: To which paragraph did you reach?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've reached approximately 168, which, in light of the Court's concerns of objections, I'm not going to ask, but that's 168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: I hope you will follow the direction of the -- the president's direction to allow us to finish this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would like to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In fact, I was just going to say that I have confirmed with Mr. Sayers again the exact numbers of the more objectionable paragraphs, and he confirmed that we have the same number, so again, with both that in mind and the Court's direction in mind, I'll go back to leading through the paragraphs fairly quickly, unless and until there is further objection. And I'll advise the witness of that as well, so we'll probably move quickly, but with a view toward the interpreters as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, you testified this morning, correct, that the proposed province 9 under the Vance-Owen Plan was this -- included Zenica, which, in contrast to provinces 8 and 10, was a Muslim majority --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- province?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your tour of duty in Central Bosnia, did you see conduct that appeared to you not only to move Muslim Bosnians out of province 10, but also to move Croats out of province 9?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in some of these instances, it involved the movement of Bosnian Croats who were living in Zenica and the surrounding villages, with the apparent purpose of increasing the Croat populations; that is, by moving these Croats and then increasing the Croat populations in Vitez and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court, is it correct that on the 24th of April, 1993, there were a lot of rumours being stated or circulated among the Bosnian Croats saying that the Muslims were going to attack and kill all of the Croats in Zenica and the small villages south, and, I might add, west of Zenica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct. We formed a team and we investigated the rumours. We even took the Catholic priest in Zenica with us in the team to do some fact-finding in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Catholic priest was Father Stjepan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I can direct your attention and the Court's attention to Exhibit 696, I'm going to handle the next several exhibits as a group, if we can, major. If you look at Exhibit 696, would you also have in front of you and look at Exhibit 698. Based on your investigation, sir, can you tell us whether -- the statements in Exhibits 696 and 698, did you find the statements in those documents to be consistent with or supported by the facts on the ground as you found them?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Actually, when we were doing our fact-finding, there was nothing there that we could relate to those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, on 696, at the first paragraph, it ends by saying that the Mujahedin forces have, quote, "even started using tanks against women and children." Did you have any evidence or have any information at the time that any Muslim forces had used tanks against women and children?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reference to paragraph -- excuse me, Exhibit 698, did you find any information to support the allegation toward the bottom of the text of that statement that 60 civilians have been massacred in the Kuber area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look next at Exhibit 708. In Exhibit 708, Colonel Blaskic makes the allegation that, again, second and third paragraphs: "In the city itself, the arresting, harassing, and robbing of civilian women and children is going on for a long time now. The men arrested are thrown under tanks."

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw no facts to support that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No. And I can remember that we asked for proofs, and they were not able to provide us with proofs, and we didn't find any proofs on this during our fact-finding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to Exhibit 718, this is a Busovaca Joint Commission report for the 18th of April, 1993. Directing your attention to paragraph 8, there was a meeting -- the members of the Busovaca or representatives of the Busovaca Joint Commission met with Mario Cerkez around that time, around the 18th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking down a couple of lines into that same paragraph, it makes a reference to the hearsay massacre in Zenica and the Kuber hills, and then he goes on to say, with apparent reference to Mr. Cerkez: "He is also concerned of BiH digging trenches near the BritBat camp." Once again, had you seen any information to support any alleged massacre around Zenica or the Kuber hills?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: No. During our fact-finding, we only found minor damage in those villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I wanted to find out: Was the fact-finding in response --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was the fact-finding in response to specific allegations of Muslim atrocities?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, every time when we had a protest or something similar, we went to that area to see if we were able to confirm the protest, to see if anything had happened or it just was a rumour or some sort of propaganda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before continuing on, if we can go back and look at Exhibit 696, the document apparently signed by Dario Kordic. This was sent to, among other things -- excuse me, among other persons or organisations, it was sent to Colonel Stewart, it was sent to Mr. Thebault, it was sent to the Red Cross in Zenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the second paragraph, Mr. Kordic and the others said, "We ask your help in organising the evacuation of the Zenica Croats to the area of Cajdras." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, what would have been the effect, in terms of the movement of populations and ethnic groups, from moving the Croats from around Zenica to further west, around to the west of Cajdras, in connection with the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. This was obvious, that the HVO wanted all the Croats out of province number 9 -- it was the Muslim province -- and move them to province number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, continuing on, please, did you find -- I'm looking now, Your Honour, at paragraph 174. Did you find, around this time, then, that there was a movement of Croats out of Zenica and the surrounding area to a location including and around the Croat village of Grahovcici? And my apologies for the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, because of all these rumours, a lot of Croats flew out of Zenica, and I think it was 2.000 Croats who went to Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to Exhibit 765, in connection with these rumours and the movement of Croats out of Zenica, did the ECMM prepare a report titled "Special Report on Croats in Zenica, 20/21 April, 1993," which has been marked as 765? I'm sorry, is that correct, sir? Was such a report prepared?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, looking at the second page, is it signed by three ECMM monitors, or at least in typed script, including yourself, "Lars"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. The other two are Torborn Juhnov, a Swedish monitor, and Remi Landry, the Canadian monitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with particular attention to paragraph number 2, did your report state -- and I'm not going to read the entire paragraph, but just to set the scene: "The following Zenica Croat suburbs were visited to clarify the housing situation and see if it was safe to have their inhabitants return," and you give a list of villages, including Cajdras; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Skipping down to about the end of that paragraph before you get to the list of villages. Is it correct, sir, that -- "In all of the villages visited, the Croats interviewed mentioned that they had received aid and protection from their Muslim neighbours during the fighting." And then you give a list after that of the damage or situation in each of those villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to item 3 on the next page, that makes reference to your trip with Father Stjepan?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 3(A): "In that village, the village was not damaged, and the local Croats told us that they were protected by their Muslim neighbours."

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to item 4, "Conclusions," did you and your team reach the conclusion that: "Except for the village of Zaljev, the damages were less than expected. Father Stjepan had been told that all of the above-mentioned villages had been destroyed and left."

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of your observations in these villages at this time, is it true and correct then that Father Stjepan agreed, a Croat, a Croat Catholic priest, agreed with your assessment?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. He asked us to help in getting the refugees or the few people back to their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm jumping ahead, based on the testimony in the last few minutes, to paragraph 181. The net results of this mission was that you found that-- you thought they -- ECMM, in an assessment with which Father Stjepan agreed, that the Bosnian Croats who had fled that area could, in fact, safely move back into their homes?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then and mister -- excuse me, Father Stjepan went to Grahovcici and arranged to meet with representatives of the Croat refugees to tell them that it was safe for them to go home?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And Morsink was there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct there were about 2.000 Croat refugees in that village?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked to the Croat refugees, is it correct that they told you that when they fled the villages, they had been told rumours or heard rumours of Muslim killings and attacks in those villages?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that those rumours had come from other Croats?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn that the various stories that were being spread around that time about alleged Muslim perpetrated massacres were being used to scare the Bosnian Croats from going back to their homes around Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Once again, I object to that sort of question. I think it's leading and it calls for opinions that are beyond the expertise of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can say, in this court, what he was told by the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 26th of April, 1993, you and Mr. Morsink and Father Stjepan developed a plan and went back to Grahovcici with the plan to transport the Croats back to their homes using some buses that Father Stjepan had actually arranged for; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir that at an HVO checkpoint at Novi Selo, the convoy was stopped and refused passage by the HVO military police?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And they it even took the buses from us and left us without the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the military police indicate to you where -- well, strike that. Is it correct that the military police said that the HVO in Travnik had ordered that all refugees be stopped from returning to their homes around Zenica and that they instead be taken to Novi Bila?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what they used our buses to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can just momentarily look back at 2574, the map from the newspaper article. If you can just put that on the ELMO, then we can refer to that rather than everyone needing to perhaps go digging for it. Sir, looking at the map which is 2574, can you look at that map and, perhaps if there's anyway to get closer, some in closer on the border between 9 and 10 -- is there anyway the video unit can do that? Thank you very much. The movement of these Croats from -- which started out around Zenica and to take them to Novi Bila, would that have the effect of moving these Croats from province 9 and into province 10?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In talking to the refugees, sir, did you learn that many of them had, in fact, wanted to return to their own homes following your visit and Father Stjepan's visit the day or two before, but they told you that when they arrived at an HVO checkpoint they were stopped and forced to go back by the HVO to Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. We had a meeting with some representatives from the refugees in Grahovcici, and they told us that some of them already tried to get back to their homes but they were stopped by HVO at checkpoints and forced back to Grahovcici. The Croat refugees told us that the HVO soldiers fired their weapons against them, to force them --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Warning shots?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, warning shots, to force them back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's correct, sir, that you and your group eventually got these buses back from the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, because we made a protest at the spot. At the same time a UNMO, United Nations military observer, came to that area and he helped us, by his radio equipment, to send this protest to someone, and after a while we got our buses back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that were you, in fact, ultimately able to arrange for approximately 1.400 of these 2.000 to be returned to their own houses back in the area around Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The rest -- I think, 300 had already been forced by HVO -- or moved by HVO to the Bila area, and 300 of them wanted to stay in Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving forward, toward the end of April --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm looking at paragraph 194, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Toward the end of April, did you engage in another series of missions now in a different part of that area in Central Bosnia, more to the south around Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that based -- that the ECMM had, during this time, developed increasing concerns about what was happening in the Muslim villages in the Kiseljak area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 27th of April, is it correct that an ECMM team consisting of you and Henk Morsink travelled to the Kiseljak area with the UNHCR and a doctor and a nurse from Medecins du Monde, under escort of two Canadian Battalion armoured personnel carriers which themselves were equipped with heavy machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you have to go with armoured personnel carriers at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Because at the time it was not safe for us to travel around the area in our soft-skinned vehicles. It happened often, almost every day, that someone shot after us, so we were not secure in our soft-skinned vehicles. Therefore, in this part we could not move without armed protection from UNPROFOR. And specifically when we were going to the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we could stop for a moment. I'm sorry, it's my fault. I missed one exhibit. Before we continue on to Kiseljak, would you just look at Exhibit 832? We'll just identify it and move on. Is Exhibit 832 a report that you prepared and bears your signature on the second page, your report for the 26th of April, 1993, which talks about your efforts to return these Bosnian Croats from the Bosnian Croat territory back to the area around Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the Court has the time to read the document, they'll see that it talks about the fact of the three -- the story about the three buses and all the rest of that story; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Now, if we can go back to Kiseljak. So you're moving around in armoured personnel carriers now because, in fact, for safety reasons it was necessary?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct then that on the 27th of April, you and Mr. Morsink went to the Rotilj near Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have reports that Muslim civilians in this village had been killed by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. That was one of the reasons that we were going to Rotilj again. There had been a team there earlier. They had reported on incidents in Rotilj, and now we went to Rotilj to see how the civilians were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: And if they still were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention to Exhibit 818. This is a report by your colleague -- well, two of your colleagues, including on the second page, Remi Landry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on the basis of Mr. Landry's report, which you can see on the top part of the first page of the report concerns the village Rotilj -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, was it largely based on his report that you organised a mission to go to Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. That was why we were bringing a nurse and a doctor and a representative from UNHCR, because they were not able to have any help because Rotilj is situated in what you would call a valley and surrounded by a hilly terrain, and on this hilly terrain the HVO had positions. So every time some of the inhabitants of Rotilj tried to go out of the village, they were shot at. So the HVO controlled that area, and so they were not able to have any food or anything else into the village. We knew from the team with Remi Landry and Dimitrios Dagos that there was a lack of help, so we went in with some help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tried to enter -- well, were you able to actually get into Rotilj that day?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Into Rotilj, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you move, on that day, to another Muslim village called Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, because we heard from UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak that they were able to see that there had been a lot of burning houses in that area, but the headquarters in Kiseljak was not able -- the UNPROFOR headquarters in Kiseljak was not able to go up there. Therefore, we went to Gomionica to monitor the situation there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. By the way, did you find the conditions that you saw in Rotilj, yourself, to be consistent and to bear out Mr. Landry's report?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. We were told exactly the same about the situation, and we were told about the incidents by the inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but to direct your attention back to Exhibit 818, what you saw when you went to Rotilj supported the allegations set forth in Mr. Landry's report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you try -- you tried to get into Gomionica, and what was the result of that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Actually, we were not allowed. We tried the first one checkpoint -- one route -- road into Gomionica, but we were stopped at the checkpoint. Then we tried another road into Gomionica and again we were stopped at a checkpoint. At this checkpoint -- both those checkpoints were manned by HVO. At the last checkpoint they gave us ten seconds to leave that area. They put up the anti-tank gun in firing positions against us and aimed all their weapons against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around that time, were you -- did the HVO commander at that particular checkpoint tell you that he had orders from the HVO commander in Kiseljak, Ivica Rajic, to close all the roads and stop all U.N. and ECMM vehicles from travelling in that area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, based upon this threat of arms, you and your team did leave the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, in the course of your testimony today, is it fair to say that in the course of your travels around Central Bosnia, you had frequent problems at HVO checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with the map that we were looking at earlier today, we also saw that there were some ABiH checkpoints. Did you have any problems moving through those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Not through those checkpoints, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving on to 1920, if we can look at Exhibit 1920, on Exhibit 1920,1, have you marked on this aerial photograph the location of the two checkpoints which you tried to -- it's actually three, I'm sorry -- that you tried to gain access through around the village of Rotilj and Gomionica --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the 26th and 27th of April?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Right. We were stopped at this checkpoint at first [indicates], and the second time we were stopped at this checkpoint [indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Which of the checkpoints -- do you recall which checkpoint it was where the officer said that he had orders from Ivica Rajic to not let U.N. vehicles move around the area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: It was in this checkpoint up here [indicates]. And this checkpoint was heavily manned. There was only a few soldiers in this checkpoint [indicates], but this checkpoint was a very heavily manned and armed checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, moving forward, then, paragraph 211: Did you and your team then try to visit the villages of Polje Visnjica and Visnjica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your group was stopped there again by HVO checkpoints and denied access to those villages?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that on that occasion the HVO soldiers placed mines on the road in front of you and took firing positions against you with rocket-propelled grenades?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. They had a lot of anti-armour mines on a rope, and they pulled this rope with the mines out in front of us. And again, they took fire positions against us with anti-armour weapons, anti-tank weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then your group, as a result of this, on that day, on the 27th of April, returned to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the result of your not being able to get into these villages? I mean, how did this affect your ability to carry out your mission that day, by being turned back at all of these various checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We were not able to carry out our task for that day, so we were not able to monitor the situation in the area. And it was obvious for us that it was because the HVO didn't want us to monitor the situation, and that indicated that something had happened in those areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 28th of April, did another ECMM team, including yourself, and again a nurse, go to the area north of Visoko to investigate the situation involving Muslim refugees in that area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find that when you moved up -- I'm going on to paragraph 214 -- that when you went to the Red Cross in Visoko, that you found that approximately 1.038 Muslim refugees had come from the Kiseljak area, including the villages of Svinjarevo, Jehovac, Gromiljak, Behrici, Gomionica, and Bilalovac, had come from that area and enrolled with the Red Cross just in the few days around that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were refugees in fact coming from the very villages that you were trying to investigate based on the allegations of Croat atrocities?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can look at Exhibit 835, is Exhibit 835 a report prepared by you and Mr. Morsink?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it bears your signature on the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this report describe your efforts to go into the villages that you described a few moments ago on the 27th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And directing your attention to the last line of -- the last sentence of what would be -- well, it's hard to describe. If you can see, maybe you can find where I'm making reference. This confirmed again, and you did include in your report, that the HVO commander, quote, "stated that his commander, Ivica Rajic, had given orders to stop all U.N./UNHCR and ECMM vehicles"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking to Exhibit 841, is this your report from the 28th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in reference to the second part of numbered paragraph 1, this records your conclusions about the 1.038 refugees coming from the Kiseljak area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Gomionica on the -- I don't know if it was the second or third time you had tried to enter the village, you did, in fact, finally succeed in entering the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that what you found when you got there is that the village was totally destroyed; all of the inhabitants had left the area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that when you left your vehicles and tried to conduct a more detailed investigation, that you and your colleagues were shot at by several bursts of automatic weapons fire?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know from which positions this automatic weapons fire came?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: From the HVO positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you once again forced to withdraw from that area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We had to do it, yes. Even if we had those APCs from CanBat, we were not allowed to return the fire at that time, because of our rules of engagement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, a very momentary story, sir: You found yourself lying in a ditch for a while, being fired at by machine guns; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get out of that situation?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Actually the two APCs -- we were not close to the APCs, but they were able, when there was a pause in the fighting, to rescue us out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the APCs came -- essentially the APCs came to you and were able to get you out of the situation?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that on the 29th of April, an ECMM team, including yourself, with, again, an armed Canadian Battalion escort, visited the Muslim villages of Polje Visnjica, Visnjica, Hercezi, Doci, and Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes. At this time we were allowed -- we could go into Gomionica without problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I suggest the court look at Exhibit 847. What I suggest, Your Honour, I think we can finish this exhibit, and we will be at least well on our way to finishing the rest of the exam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is 847 a copy of your report, along with Mr. Laustsen --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on the 29th of April?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you signed the bottom?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The conclusions I will let, I think, speak for themselves in 2, in your findings in paragraph 2 about village-by-village -- going to the protest, can you tell the Court what had happened in connection with the HVO checkpoint about which you lodged a complaint?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: We were stopped in the checkpoint at Polje Visnjica, and our interpreter, who was a young Muslim man, was taken out of our vehicle and was threatened -- and they told him that -- actually, they wanted to shoot him, but they didn't because we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of your mission on that day, directing your attention to paragraph 4, would you just simply read that into the record, please.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: Paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: "Team conclusion, it is obvious that an ethnic cleansing had taken place in that area."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I propose we stop there, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott. You'll start again, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- at 219, and you have four more pages to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think we've moved, if I may say so, I think very quickly with a very major witness. We'll try to continue doing so. We're trying to move as fast as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, clearly we've moved with some speed. Perhaps I can say to the Defence I hope that can be kept up tomorrow. You will have the best part of the morning in which to cross-examine. If possible, the witness should get away. It is unfair on witnesses to have to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I agree that it's unfair for witnesses to have to come back, but this witness has given a colossal number of opinions today, and we're going to have to cross-examine him on those, and I do not think that we will be through in half a day. Perhaps one day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know, we must speed the cross-examinations up. I know this is an important witness, and I know that -- and I'm not criticising you in particular, Mr. Sayers, but when a witness takes a certain amount of time in chief, it's quite wrong that the cross-examination should take sometimes 50 per cent longer. There is a Rule here that cross-examination should be limited purely to matters which were covered in examination-in-chief, or direct examination, and I think that rule has got to be followed more closely. And I shall be certainly watching out for that. Of course you must have time to put your case and to cross-examine an important witness fully, but we must make as much progress as we can, and if possible, I suggest we try and finish the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I agree entirely, Your Honour, and I think that we've been through with many of the witnesses -- there have been about 50 witnesses who have testified, much of the background material, and I will try assiduously to avoid reploughing that territory which has been ploughed very many times. I'm going to try to bore in on the opinions that this witness has given, and the grounds for them, with the Trial Chamber's permission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I agree that he's covered a lot of territory, and we have covered it quickly today, but let's keep it up tomorrow. Half past 9.00. Major, would you be back, please, at half past 9.00 tomorrow, to continue with your evidence.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
utterances.text: I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN
